prompts.text: Which song became more meaningful after you heard it with friends?
Tell us about an ordinary journey that a shared playlist made unforgettable.
Each friend picks one song for the drive or one person curates the whole soundtrack?
We have fifteen minutes before leaving for a trip. How would we agree on the first three songs?
A song can remind several people of the same day for completely different reasons.
The most memorable group soundtrack isn't necessarily the one with the biggest hits.
What track reminds you of a friendship that began unexpectedly?
Recall someone choosing music that matched the group's mood better than you expected.
Everyone contributes one track to a friendship time capsule. What would you choose and why?
A playlist of songs we discovered together or one filled with our oldest favourites?
What local sound or musical tradition makes you feel connected to where you grew up?
Describe hearing music from home in an unfamiliar place.
Explore a traditional instrument together or learn the history of a popular local rhythm?
A visiting friend asks us to play music that represents our city. What range of sounds should we include?
The music people associate with a place often reaches far beyond its famous artists.
An unfamiliar regional song can tell a good story even when you don't understand every word.
Which artist from your home region deserves to be heard more widely?
Recall learning the meaning of a local song from an older relative or neighbour.
We're helping a new resident discover the city's music scene. Where would we begin?
Attend a small local performance or watch musicians explain how they make their music?
Which album have you enjoyed most when listening from beginning to end?
Tell us about changing your mind on a record after giving it a second listen.
Play an album without interruptions or discuss each track as we go?
Two friends pick very different albums for the same evening. How could we give both a fair listen?
Some records reward quiet attention more than a quick search for a catchy chorus.
A favourite album doesn't need every track to be equally strong.
What opening song makes an album feel like it has a clear direction?
Recall somebody pointing out a musical detail you'd missed on an album you knew well.
We're each asked to recommend one complete record to a friend who rarely listens to albums. What would guide our choices?
Revisit an album from our teenage years or discover a recent release together?
What's the first live performance you remember genuinely enjoying?
Describe arriving at a concert without knowing the artist and leaving impressed.
A small acoustic set where we hear every detail or a lively outdoor performance with friends?
Our group has tickets, but one person prefers to avoid the crowd. How should we plan the evening?
Live music changes how familiar songs feel when performers respond to the audience.
The best concert memory can come from the company rather than the most expensive seats.
Which song would you love to hear performed with only one instrument?
Recall a performer unexpectedly changing the arrangement of a song you knew.
A friend is attending their first concert. What would you tell them to bring or expect?
Stand close to the performance or sit somewhere comfortable with a clear view?
Which instrument would you learn if you had a friend willing to practise with you?
Tell us about seeing somebody play an instrument in a way that made it look effortless.
Learn basic keyboard chords or try simple guitar patterns as beginners?
We've borrowed an instrument for one afternoon. How would we explore it without pretending to be experts?
Watching a musician practise can teach more about patience than watching a finished performance.
Playing one song well with friends can be more satisfying than learning fragments of twenty.
Which sound would you want to understand how a musician produces?
Recall learning the difference between two instruments that you'd always confused.
A friend asks what makes an instrument difficult to learn. What would you want a player to demonstrate?
Attend a friendly beginner workshop or watch an instrumentalist explain their process?
When have friends introduced you to a genre you wouldn't have explored alone?
Describe a recommendation that seemed outside your taste until you heard the right track.
Trade songs from unfamiliar genres or each defend a guilty pleasure from our playlists?
We make a listening game where nobody can mention a song's genre until it finishes. What would we learn?
People often have wider musical tastes than the labels they use for themselves.
It's easier to discover music when you don't have to pretend to like every recommendation.
What genre do you understand better now than when you first heard it?
Recall a song that helped you appreciate a style you'd previously ignored.
Someone in our group dislikes a genre the rest of us enjoy. How could we explore the difference without arguing?
Hear one artist's influences or trace how a musical style changed over decades?
What's a piece of music you associate with a particular time of day?
Tell us about a morning when background music completely changed your mood.
Start a relaxed weekend with soft instrumentals or upbeat songs that make everyone move?
We're preparing dinner together and want music that doesn't drown out conversation. What would you play?
The same song can feel energising one day and soothing on another.
A playlist should suit what people are doing rather than how trendy the tracks are.
Which sound helps you settle into reading or focused work?
Recall hearing a song that made a long, ordinary task feel easier.
Our shared workspace has different music preferences. What listening rules would keep everyone comfortable?
A quiet playlist in the background or take turns choosing one featured song?
What makes a musical collaboration between friends sound genuine?
Describe a recording where different artists brought out unexpected qualities in one another.
Listen to a duet with distinct voices or a group performance built around harmonies?
We're asked to make a two-minute musical performance with no recording experience. How would we divide the roles?
Collaborations are more interesting when the musicians leave room for one another's styles.
A good featured artist should add something beyond a recognisable name.
Which two artists would you pair for a collaboration based on their different strengths?
Recall noticing a backing vocal or instrumental part that made an entire song work.
We want to understand how a track was arranged. Which part should we listen to in isolation first?
Watch musicians rehearse together or hear them discuss the finished track afterwards?
Which kind of songwriting story makes you appreciate a song more?
Tell us about learning the inspiration behind a track and hearing it differently afterwards.
Discuss a song's storytelling or focus on its melody and production?
We each choose a song with a strong message but different musical styles. What would we compare?
A person's relationship to a song can shift as their own experiences change.
A simple lyric can be effective without trying to sound complicated.
What's a topic you wish more musicians explored in ordinary, relatable language?
Recall a song that encouraged an interesting conversation among your friends.
A friend loves a song whose message you interpret differently. How would you compare interpretations?
Hear a songwriter explain their creative decisions or listen without knowing any background?
What's a musical memory from a family celebration that still makes you smile?
Describe somebody unexpectedly becoming the best dancer at an otherwise quiet gathering.
Keep the original music from a favourite celebration or recreate the atmosphere with new songs?
We are building a playlist for a reunion across several generations. How should we make space for everyone?
Celebrations create shared musical memories even between people with little overlap in taste.
A well-timed familiar song can mean more than a professionally mixed set.
Which song gets relatives or friends singing together almost immediately?
Recall learning a dance or chorus from somebody older at a gathering.
Our friends are hosting a relaxed reunion with limited space. What kind of music would suit it?
A friendly karaoke round or a playlist where everyone explains one memory?
